── Deep Analysis ───────────────────────────────
We are on the right side today: all three opens are LONG in a LONG_BIAS regime with BTC pinned above EMA300, and no short is open. The 24h loss of -0.59 is fully explained by two self-inflicted buckets, not by direction: 4 shorts fired against a rising tape (-0.33, 0/4) and chop entries that never confirmed (-0.37 hard_max_loss, -0.44 atr_sl_hit). The winning side for every one of those was the same coin going the other way or nothing at all — BTC ran +2.10% since the 01:13 short entry that stopped us out, and the COMP short that lost -5.7% closed +0.16% above where we shorted it.

Direction is not the discriminator and RSI is not either (7d losers cluster mid-band 45-65; 24h winners span 22-73 on meta_rsi). The discriminator is confirmation: entries that reach +0.40% and let the trail arm win 85% of the time, entries that do not lose 97% of the time. That is the trend-versus-chop line, and everything in the pending queue this cycle — 5 pump-chain- shorts, a rsi=100 SUSHI print, a ranging-coin NEO bounce — sits on the chop side of it.

1. Block shorts while BTC holds EMA300 AND 15m reads LONG_BIAS — pending GRASS/GMX/KPEPE/FOGO/BANANA shorts are the P1 pattern recurring in real time.
2. Treat trail-arm confirm as the entry: no size on any signal that has not printed +0.40% (85T/3.5% WR vs 48T/85.4% WR).
3. Downsize or tightly-invalidate STX (r2v2-long4 0/3, EXTREME vol) and stand aside on NEO-style ranging bounces; hold BTC untouched until +2%, then breakeven at 86317.
4. Reallocate idle slots only into trail-confirming LONGs with fresh price data — that is where the +3.37 is coming from.
